businessModel: Donation-funded open-source project; no ads or tracking
updateCadence: Tracks Firefox releases (about every 4 weeks) plus point releases
summary: Community Firefox fork for Android that continues Mull: Mozilla telemetry stripped, strict tracking protection, content blocking on by default, Fission site isolation. Not on Google Play: use Accrescent, its F-Droid repo or Obtainium.
bestFor: Android users wanting a hardened Firefox with no Google services
notFor: People who want one-tap Google Play installs
Those who want maximum site compatibility
Users wanting a big, long-established team

pros.title: Mull successor
pros.detail: Carries all of Mull's privacy patches and adds more from the Phoenix project.

pros.title: Telemetry stripped
pros.detail: Removes Mozilla data-collection hooks and services like Pocket while keeping E2EE sync.

pros.title: Blocking on by default
pros.detail: Reviews report built-in content blocking and strict tracking protection.

pros.title: Secure install options
pros.detail: Accrescent recommended, signing certificate fingerprint published, Obtainium supported.

pros.title: Fully open source
pros.detail: Developed on GitLab with GitHub and Codeberg mirrors.

cons.title: Not on Google Play
cons.detail: Install needs Accrescent, F-Droid repo, Obtainium or APK; no official F-Droid inclusion (project declines it).

cons.title: Site breakage
cons.detail: Hardening can break some sites and reduce features such as WebGL until re-enabled.

cons.title: Small volunteer team
cons.detail: PrivacyTools notes security-fix speed depends on a few maintainers.

faq.a: No. Use Accrescent (recommended), the project F-Droid repo, Obtainium or direct APK.

faq.q: What is its relation to Mull?
faq.a: It is a fork of Mull, which ended with DivestOS in Dec 2024; IronFox appeared in Jan 2025.
Android 5 (API 21); arm64, armv7 and x86_64 builds exist.

switching.note: Firefox Sync account works; manual import from other apps.
